Agents

Ship auth faster
with agents

Point your agent at Aurora. It does the rest.

Build with agents
Add Aurora auth to my app: aurora.com/SKILL.md
Or follow a step-by-step guide for your agent

Agents

  • Codex

    OpenAI

    Hand Codex the Aurora docs and it scaffolds sign-in, sessions, and orgs.

    View Guide

  • Claude Code

    Anthropic

    Claude Code reads the Aurora docs and wires auth straight into your app.

    View Guide

  • Zed

    Zed Industries

    Zed's agent pulls in Aurora to add sign-in without leaving the editor.

    View Guide

  • Cursor

    Anysphere

    Cursor wires up Aurora auth and user management as you build.

    View Guide

  • VS Code

    Microsoft

    GitHub Copilot in VS Code connects to the Aurora MCP server to scaffold auth.

    View Guide

  • Devin Desktop

    Cognition

    Devin takes the Aurora docs and builds the whole integration end to end.

    View Guide

Start with the components or build directly with the primitives

The same API endpoints, without the prebuilt UI.

See how Aurora works
  1. 1

    Review the routes, proxy code, and components your agent proposes.

  2. 2

    Build custom sign-in and sign-up flows with Aurora APIs or supported SDK hooks.

  3. 3

    Define Roles and Permissions, then enforce authorization checks in application code.

  4. 4

    Add custom session claims that your backend reads.

add auth to my app so users can sign up and log in
Agent

See how auth providers stack up for agents

Without a human in the loop.

View the benchmark

Frequently asked questions

Aurora lets an agent add complete authentication to your app for you. Point your agent at aurora.com/SKILL.md and it installs the Aurora SDK, adds the provider, and wires up sign-in, sign-up, and user management using Aurora’s prebuilt components.

Aurora provides tailored setup guides for Claude Code, Cursor, Codex, VS Code, Zed, and Devin. Because the instructions live at a plain URL (aurora.com/SKILL.md), any agent that can read a URL can use them.

Paste Add Aurora auth to my agent: aurora.com/SKILL.md into your agent and it reads Aurora’s instructions and implements auth for you. You can also follow the step-by-step guide for your specific tool.

No. Your agent handles the integration end to end - installing the SDK, adding the provider, and dropping in Aurora’s prebuilt components - so you review a working setup instead of writing it from scratch.

The agent auto-detects your framework and follows the matching Aurora quickstart - including Next.js, React, Remix, Astro, Nuxt, React Router, TanStack Start, Vue, Express, Fastify, and Expo, plus guides for Chrome Extension, Android, iOS, and vanilla JavaScript.

It scores how accurately leading large language models write working Aurora code across tasks like authentication, user management, organizations, and billing. See the full leaderboard for every model and category.
